reason: A offers the more substantive extension of prior work by testing Ag-enabled reactive wear protection across temperature while measuring both friction and wear; its proposed oxide–Ag tribolayer is physically more plausible at elevated temperatures, although the cited evidence directly supports wear reduction more strongly than friction reduction. B largely repeats the cited 2D-HEA spray-coating approach and relies on ethanol-derived amorphous carbon remaining available and stable up to 600 °C in air, which is poorly supported and physically doubtful.
